name: Scrum Practice
description: An agile framework that helps teams generate value through adaptive solutions for complex problems, mapped to the foundational Platform Adoption Kernel. It establishes the empirical process control required for modern platform engineering.

alphas.name: Sprint
alphas.description: A time-boxed iteration of continuous development and value delivery, typically 1-4 weeks in duration.

states.name: Planned
states.description: The Sprint Goal has been defined and the Sprint Backlog is committed by the team.

checklist.name: Capacity Established
checklist.description: Team availability, holidays, and total capacity are calculated and transparent.

checklist.name: Sprint Goal Formulated
checklist.description: A clear, concise Sprint Goal is agreed upon by the Scrum Team.

checklist.name: Commitment Made
checklist.description: The developers explicitly commit to the Sprint Backlog scope.

states.name: Active
states.description: The Sprint is currently in progress, with daily inspection and adaptation.

checklist.name: Daily Syncs Occurring
checklist.description: The Daily Scrum is held every working day to inspect progress toward the Sprint Goal.

checklist.name: Continuous Integration
checklist.description: Work is continuously integrated, tested, and added to the Increment.

checklist.name: Impediments Addressed
checklist.description: Blockers identified in the Daily Scrum are actively resolved by the Scrum Master.

states.name: Reviewed
states.description: The outcome of the Sprint has been demonstrated to stakeholders for feedback.

checklist.name: Increment Demonstrated
checklist.description: Working, "Done" software is demonstrated to key stakeholders.

checklist.name: Feedback Captured
checklist.description: Stakeholder feedback and market shifts are recorded to influence the next Product Backlog refinement.

states.name: Retrospected
states.description: The team has reflected on their performance and identified process improvements.

checklist.name: Metrics Analyzed
checklist.description: Velocity, burn-down charts, and quality metrics are reviewed.

checklist.name: Process Friction Identified
checklist.description: Team members candidly discuss what went well and what caused friction.

checklist.name: Action Items Created
checklist.description: Concrete process improvements are added to the backlog for the next Sprint.

workProducts.name: Product Backlog
workProducts.description: An emergent, ordered list of what is needed to improve the product. It is the single source of work undertaken by the Scrum Team.

levelsOfDetail.name: Initiated
levelsOfDetail.description: Items are added to the backlog as rough concepts or epics.

checklist.name: Items Drafted
checklist.description: Product Backlog Items (PBIs) are drafted with basic descriptions.

checklist.name: Business Value Proposed
checklist.description: Initial business value hypotheses are associated with the items.

levelsOfDetail.name: Refined
levelsOfDetail.description: Items are sized, clarified, and acceptance criteria are added.

checklist.name: Acceptance Criteria Added
checklist.description: Clear conditions of satisfaction are defined for the PBIs.

checklist.name: Estimated
checklist.description: Items are estimated by the development team (e.g., using story points).

levelsOfDetail.name: Ready For Sprint
levelsOfDetail.description: Items at the top of the backlog are clear, ordered, and small enough to be completed in one Sprint.

checklist.name: Ordered
checklist.description: The Product Owner has prioritized the items based on maximum business value.

checklist.name: Sized Appropriately
checklist.description: The items are broken down enough to confidently fit into a single Sprint boundary.

workProducts.name: Sprint Backlog
workProducts.description: The set of Product Backlog items selected for the Sprint, plus a plan for delivering the Increment.

levelsOfDetail.name: Planned
levelsOfDetail.description: The initial scope and tactical execution plan for the Sprint is documented.

checklist.name: Sprint Goal Visibile
checklist.description: The Sprint Goal is documented at the top of the backlog.

checklist.name: Tasks Broken Down
checklist.description: Selected PBIs are broken down into actionable technical tasks.

levelsOfDetail.name: Active
levelsOfDetail.description: The backlog is being dynamically updated as work progresses.

checklist.name: Daily State Updates
checklist.description: Task states (e.g., To Do, Doing, Done) are updated continuously.

checklist.name: Scope Negotiated
checklist.description: If capacity changes, the developers negotiate scope boundaries with the Product Owner.

levelsOfDetail.name: Completed
levelsOfDetail.description: The time-box has expired and the Sprint Backlog is retired.

checklist.name: Remaining Work Moved
checklist.description: Any incomplete work is moved back to the Product Backlog.

checklist.name: Done Work Validated
checklist.description: All completed tasks meet the Definition of Done.

workProducts.name: Increment
workProducts.description: The concrete stepping stone toward the Product Goal. Each Increment is additive to all prior Increments.

levelsOfDetail.name: Integrated
levelsOfDetail.description: The new features and artifacts have been merged with existing components.

checklist.name: Build Successful
checklist.description: The continuous integration pipeline compiles the Increment without errors.

checklist.name: Automated Tests Passed
checklist.description: All unit and integration tests return green.

levelsOfDetail.name: Done
levelsOfDetail.description: The Increment formally meets the strict Definition of Done and is fully operational.

checklist.name: Definition of Done Met
checklist.description: The organization's strict quality and security gates have been satisfied.

checklist.name: Deployable
checklist.description: The artifact is successfully packaged and ready for immediate deployment to production.

activities.name: Refine Product Backlog
activities.description: The ongoing activity of adding detail, estimates, and order to items in the Product Backlog.

activities.name: Conduct Sprint Planning
activities.description: Initiates the Sprint by laying out the work to be performed. The Scrum Team determines the why, what, and how.

activities.name: Hold Daily Scrum
activities.description: A 15-minute daily event to inspect progress toward the Sprint Goal and adapt the Sprint Backlog as necessary.

activities.name: Conduct Sprint Review
activities.description: Inspect the outcome of the Sprint and determine future adaptations.

activities.name: Conduct Sprint Retrospective
activities.description: Plan ways to increase quality and effectiveness. The team inspects how the last Sprint went with regards to individuals, interactions, processes, tools, and their Definition of Done.

patterns.name: Scrum Sprint Lifecycle
patterns.description: The sequential phase model orchestrating the cadence of empirical delivery over a single iteration.

patternViews.name: Sprint Planning Phase
patternViews.description: The focused phase for establishing scope and tactical alignment before execution begins.

patternViews.name: Sprint Execution Phase
patternViews.description: The core iteration phase focused on daily alignment and engineering value generation.

patternViews.name: Sprint Review Phase
patternViews.description: The focused phase for market evaluation and stakeholder value alignment.

patternViews.name: Sprint Retrospective Phase
patternViews.description: The terminal phase of the iteration dedicated purely to continuous team improvement.

workBreakdowns.name: Scrum Execution Schedule
workBreakdowns.description: The operational execution structures and discrete tasks required to fulfill a single Sprint iteration.

complexity.name: Sprint Delivery Complexity
complexity.description: Algorithmic modifiers applied based on standard iteration risk vectors.

task.name: Execute Capacity Planning
task.description: Calculate team velocity constraints and map available working hours for the upcoming iteration.

task.name: Facilitate Daily Standup
task.description: Execute the 15-minute timebox requiring developers to state progress, intentions, and immediate blockers.

task.name: Host Demo and Review
task.description: Present the Increment to external stakeholders and gather actionable feedback to adjust the Product Backlog.

task.name: Perform Iteration Retrospective
task.description: Analyze team metrics and friction points, establishing at least one concrete action item for process enhancement.
